summary: Three UI lighting looks in one component: sweeping shine, rim glow, and normal-mapped shading.
overview: Drop it on any UI Graphic and pick a mode. One shared shader implements all three, so switching mode is a dropdown rather than a different material. Scene Light mode reacts to the real directional light, via the scene hook.
useCases: A shine sweeping across a button to draw attention.
A rim glow marking a selected or equipped item.
Normal-mapped UI that catches the scene's light.

params.tuning: Shine, Rim and Scene Light are mutually exclusive. Most of the other settings only apply to one of them.
45 matches the conventional diagonal shine. Zero sweeps horizontally, which reads as a scanline.
Scene Light mode needs a real normal map to look like anything other than flat shading.

gotchas.title: Most settings are mode-specific
gotchas.body: Adjusting a rim setting in Shine mode changes nothing. Expected, and confusing in a long Inspector.

gotchas.title: Scene Light mode needs the hook in the scene
gotchas.body: Without SceneLightUIHook the direction is a default, so the shading will not match the world.
